builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DealsFlow: An Evidence-Gated Agentic Harness for Venture Capital Deal Triage
summary: Replaces direct LLM-emitted investment scores with a pipeline in which the model cites evidence and rates categories while deterministic code caps and only lowers scores, via a corroboration ceiling, a lower-only sceptic call, and pre-fetched evidence retrieval. Costs an extra sceptic generation pass plus evidence retrieval and indexing latency, and 70% of reports still need analyst correction, so human review time is retained. Can fail through non-date-restricted retrieval leaking future information (the reported correlations may overstate screening skill), through the untested lower-only sceptic rule, and through residual unsupported claims (16% of citations not fully supported).
rationale: The harness runs on a single API-accessible LLM with modest retrieval infrastructure, the design patterns (evidence gating, score ceilings, sceptic pass) transfer directly to any high-stakes LLM scoring workflow, and the authors themselves report the gains are small, so adoption should target auditability and time savings rather than accuracy.
technique: Evidence-gated LLM scoring harness with sceptic pass

claims.statement: Replaces direct LLM-emitted investment scores with a pipeline in which the model cites evidence and rates categories while deterministic code caps and only lowers scores, via a corroboration ceiling, a lower-only sceptic call, and pre-fetched evidence retrieval. Costs an extra sceptic generation pass plus evidence retrieval and indexing latency, and 70% of reports still need analyst correction, so human review time is retained. Can fail through non-date-restricted retrieval leaking future information (the reported correlations may overstate screening skill), through the untested lower-only sceptic rule, and through residual unsupported claims (16% of citations not fully supported).
Spearman rho improved from 0.38 (unconstrained LLM) to 0.45 (95% CI 0.32-0.57) and write-off AUC from 0.68 to 0.71; analyst time per application fell from 44.7 to 18.9 minutes.
